chunks: From him, from al-Ḥasan, from Zur‘ah, from Samā‘ah, who said:

Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام gave judgment regarding a man who struck a غلام on his head, so part of his tongue was affected, and he could articulate some speech but could not articulate some of it. So he had him recite the alphabet, then apportioned the diyah against him: whatever he could articulate, he excluded it, and whatever he could not articulate, he made him liable for it.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَا: Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام in his judicial capacity
key_terms.الْمُعْجَمَ: the alphabet used to test articulation
key_terms.غُلَامًا: a young boy or servant who was injured
key_terms.لِسَانِهِ: his tongue, meaning his faculty of speech

ai.seo_question: How is diyah calculated for partial loss of speech after an injury in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal ruling of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام concerning partial speech impairment caused by injury. Compensation was assessed proportionally by testing which letters the injured person could still pronounce and which he could no longer articulate.
